summary.title: The Twelve-Factor App
summary.one_liner: A methodology of twelve principles for building software-as-a-service apps that are portable, deployable on cloud platforms, and scalable.
takeaways: The twelve-factor methodology targets software-as-a-service apps built for modern cloud platforms.
Key goals include declarative setup, a clean contract with the OS for portability, and minimal divergence between development and production.
The methodology applies to apps in any programming language and any combination of backing services such as databases, queues, or memory caches.
The guidance is based on the authors' experience deploying hundreds of apps and observing hundreds of thousands via the Heroku platform.
The page is only an introduction; the individual twelve factors are not included in the text provided.
summary.summary: This page introduces the Twelve-Factor App, a methodology for building software-as-a-service web apps. It lists the goals: declarative setup for new developers, a clean contract with the operating system for portability, suitability for modern cloud platforms, dev/prod parity for continuous deployment, and scaling without major changes. The authors say it synthesizes their experience from the Heroku platform and is inspired by Martin Fowler's books. The text provided covers only the introduction and background, so the individual factors are not described here.
